overview: Sprouts Farmers Market is a specialty grocery retailer focused on fresh produce and natural/organic, attribute-driven products, operating 504 stores in 25 states (September 27, 2026) after a record 15 openings in Q3. It sits between conventional supermarkets and premium natural grocers such as Whole Foods, with self-distributed produce, a growing Sprouts Brand (about 26% of sales) and e-commerce above 16% of sales. After a blockbuster FY2025 (net sales $8,806M, comps +7.3%, diluted EPS $5.31), comps turned negative in 2026 (Q1 -1.7%, Q2 -1.0%, Q3 -0.9%, driven by a 3.3% fall in transactions); on October 28, 2026 management cut FY2026 guidance sharply (EPS about $4.80 vs $5.32-$5.40 prior), guided Q4 comps to -2% to -4% and announced a larger affordability price investment from Q4 into FY2027, sending the stock down about 23% to a two-year low.

business_model.summary: Specialty grocery with emphasis on fresh produce and natural/organic products. Revenue is almost entirely in-store plus e-commerce (third-party delivery via Instacart, DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Shipt, with e-commerce sales up 12% in Q3 to over 16% of sales); no wholesale or franchise. Perishables are about 57% and non-perishables about 43% of sales (YTD FY2026). Sprouts Brand private label is about 26% of sales. The company self-distributes produce and, since 2025, meat and seafood through its fresh distribution centers (about 80% of stores within 250 miles of a DC). Q3 FY2026 gross margin was 38.2% (-50 bps YoY on shrink of about 40 bps and fuel of about 10 bps); SG&A was 29.6% of sales.

revenue_streams.name: Perishables (produce, meat, seafood, deli, bakery, dairy)

business_model.customer_type: B2C focused on two target segments: health enthusiasts (core) and selective shoppers. Millennials and Gen Z over-index. Often a secondary shopping destination, so basket and visit frequency are sensitive to budget pressure. Management says the less-engaged customer shows the largest leakage and that core customers have only recently begun to soften.
business_model.geographic_mix: Heavy West Coast and Sun Belt concentration (California is the largest state, then Texas, Arizona, Florida, Colorado) with expansion into the Southeast, Mid-Atlantic and Northeast. 504 stores in 25 states at September 27, 2026 (first New York store opened January 2026; 500th store in The Woodlands, TX in September 2026).

competitive_position.market_position: Specialty natural/organic grocer positioned between Trader Joe's (value) and Whole Foods (premium), with a smaller store box (about 21k-25k sq ft). Share is being lost at the margin to discount and club formats: press commentary cites Walmart (+2.6% comps) and Costco (+6%+ comps) gaining while Sprouts and Kroger stagnate. On the Q3 call, incoming CEO Nick Konat said affordability is now a bigger driver of store choice and that the current pricing strategy 'has not delivered', with competition intensifying from both natural/organic and conventional retailers chasing health-focused shoppers.

moat_factors.description: Over 70% of sales from attribute-driven products (organic, plant-based, gluten-free) and constant innovation. Still anchors the core health-enthusiast customer, but weaker traffic shows the assortment alone is not enough when price perception is unfavorable.

moat_factors.factor: Produce expertise and self-distribution supply chain
moat_factors.description: Self-distributes produce, meat and seafood through regional fresh DCs, giving freshness and cost control that conventional peers lack. Management lists further self-distribution as a margin recovery lever.
About 26% of sales and growing faster than the business; exclusive and margin-accretive. Management is using entry-price Sprouts Brand items (cage-free eggs, raw almonds) as price-perception anchors.
About one year into the chainwide launch; management says it has 'barely cracked the surface' of first-party data use for personalization and merchandising. Not yet visible in traffic.

moat_factors.factor: Efficient small-box format and new-store returns
moat_factors.description: Smaller stores need less capital and deliver faster paybacks; new stores contributed $128.8M of Q3 sales. Recent classes are described as performing strongly, though ROIC (including operating leases) has slipped to 16.1% from 18.3% on a trailing basis.

weaknesses: Comparable transactions have fallen about 3.3-3.4% for the year to date; management says 'traffic, units and frequency are not recovering, even against easier compares', which undercuts the 'tough comparisons' explanation
Management concedes current pricing strategy is not delivering and price perception is a problem; a broader price reset is planned (January 2027), which will pressure margins before it helps traffic
Shrink is elevated (about 40 bps of sales headwind in Q3) and fuel costs are a gross margin drag
California and Sun Belt concentration create regulatory, climate and regional-competition (for example H-E-B in Texas) exposure
Leadership turnover at the top and in technology: CEO transition on January 4, 2027, and the CTO left on October 12, 2026 with no named successor
Smaller scale than Walmart, Costco, Kroger and Albertsons limits purchasing power outside produce

growth_drivers: Unit growth: 42 net new stores planned for FY2026 (28 opened and 1 closed YTD; record 15 openings in Q3), pipeline of 105 executed leases and over 160 approved sites; long-term aspiration of about 10% annual unit growth. Management declined to give FY2027 unit guidance and said it must 'balance that with the other needs of the business', so the 2027 pace is uncertain.

Affordability reset: a 'more meaningful price investment across a broader range of products' (entry points, trust-builders such as conventional produce, key value items such as organic grass-fed beef) beginning in Q4 FY2026 with a broader pricing reset in January 2027. Intended to restore traffic; success unproven and it costs margin first (about 90 bps gross margin deleverage guided for Q4).
E-commerce: sales grew 12% in Q3 and exceed 16% of total sales, aided by the Shipt expansion; incremental reach without store capital but with platform fees.
Private label and loyalty personalization: Sprouts Brand at about 26% of sales and Sprouts Rewards first-party data to drive targeted offers and merchandising.

Supply chain self-help: completed meat/seafood self-distribution, retail media growth, vendor partnerships and sourcing initiatives cited as margin offsets; management committed to keep EBIT margin above 5% in FY2027 while funding price, technology and labor.
Cyclospora normalization and easier comparisons: the outbreak cost about 0.6 pt of Q3 comps and began to ease, but Q4 FY2026 is guided worse (-2% to -4%), so the lapping argument is weakening.
Secular health-and-wellness demand for better-for-you food, although discount-channel competition and value-seeking behavior are offsetting it.

business.description: Comps were -1.7%, -1.0% and -0.9% in Q1-Q3 FY2026 with transactions down 3.3%; Q4 is guided to -2% to -4%. Because traffic is not recovering against easier compares, the slowdown looks partly structural (price perception, competition) rather than only a lapping effect.

business.risk: Price investment may not restore traffic
business.description: Management admits the current pricing strategy has not worked and is moving to broader affordability investments with the pace subject to customer response. Risk that margin is sacrificed without a comp inflection.

Walmart, Costco, Aldi and Kroger are expanding better-for-you assortments at lower prices; Whole Foods, Trader Joe's and regional players (H-E-B) compete on produce and value. Secondary-destination status makes Sprouts easy to substitute.

Shrink added about 40 bps of sales headwind in Q3 and about 30 bps year to date; management says it is 'not where we want it to be' and persists into Q4 as sales are soft and product disruptions continue.

The 2026 cyclospora outbreak on lettuce and salads reduced Q3 comps by about 0.6 pt. Perishables are 57% of sales and sourcing is California-heavy, so weather, disease and recalls can hit sales abruptly.

financial.description: FY2026 EBIT guidance is about $605M (YTD EBIT $542M, down 4%, so Q4 EBIT is only about $63M including a 53rd week); Q4 gross margin faces about 90 bps of price-investment deleverage on top of shrink and fuel. 10-Q: 'investments, together with lower comparable store sales, to pressure our margins in the near term'. Net income margin was 4.9% in Q3 versus 5.5%.

FY2026 capex is about $310M net of landlord reimbursements (top of the earlier $280-310M range) versus $224M in FY2025, with operating cash flow of $555M for 39 weeks (down 4%). Buybacks were $302M YTD at an average of $77.65, well above the current share price, with $537M authorization remaining; a further $30M was bought through October 26. Cash is $229M and the $600M revolver is undrawn, so liquidity is fine but flexibility between store growth and buybacks narrows.

financial.risk: Returns on invested capital drifting lower
financial.description: ROIC including leases fell to 16.1% from 18.3% as average property and equipment rose about 24% while NOPAT slipped. Weaker new-store productivity or slower openings would feed through to the growth thesis.

regulatory.risk: Securities class action and derivative suits
regulatory.description: A Section 10(b) class action (Singh Family Revocable Trust) filed November 2025 in the District of Arizona over statements about customer resilience; lead plaintiff appointed September 4, 2026, amended complaint due November 10, 2026. Related derivative suits are stayed. No loss accrual; a new guidance cut could prompt additional filings.
California minimum wage and scheduling/benefit mandates affect a large share of team members; management is also planning labor investments in FY2027.
FDA, USDA and state rules on organic standards, labeling and food safety (FSMA) apply to expanding private label and self-distributed fresh categories.
Loyalty program and personalization expand customer data collection, raising CPRA and state privacy compliance obligations.

macro.description: Management cites a 'challenging consumer environment' and lower traffic with 'more measured spending'. The less-engaged shopper is leaking fastest to discount and club formats.
Higher fuel costs added about 10 bps to Q3 gross margin pressure and persist into Q4; produce prices, tariffs and labor costs also matter.
Wildfire, drought and heat risk to the California produce supply chain and store base.

execution.description: Jack Sinclair becomes executive chairman and Nick Konat (President/COO) becomes CEO on January 4, 2027, just as a broad price reset launches. Konat is already fronting the reset on the call, so continuity is high but accountability for a failed reset is shared.

CTO James Bahrenburg stepped down on October 12, 2026 (not due to disagreement; advisor through March 31, 2027; no successor named) while the company is increasing technology investment for personalization and efficiency.
Record opening cadence in unfamiliar Northeast and Mid-Atlantic markets, with transactions already falling in the existing base, raises cannibalization and productivity risk.
Third-party platform fees ($8.1M YTD increase) and platform dependence.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. natural/organic food demand continues to grow, but the share is increasingly contested by conventional and discount grocers who have expanded better-for-you and private-label ranges. Grocery traffic is shifting toward value formats (Walmart, Costco, Aldi) amid a cautious consumer; Kroger is also reporting minimal comp growth. The 2026 cyclospora outbreak temporarily depressed fresh produce demand industry-wide (also hurting salad restaurants such as Sweetgreen).
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate for food at home, but higher than conventional grocers because Sprouts is a premium-priced, often secondary destination. 2026 shows traffic sensitivity: basket size is up about 2.5% while transactions are down about 3.3%.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity: no funded debt, $600M undrawn revolver; net interest swung to a small expense (finance leases) from income as cash was spent on buybacks. Indirect via consumer budgets and new-store lease costs.
key_input_costs: Fresh produce (weather, disease, water availability, California sourcing)
Labor (California minimum wage, planned labor investment in FY2027)
Fuel and energy (transport and refrigeration; cited as a gross margin headwind in Q3 and Q4)
Real estate and occupancy across 500+ stores (landlord reimbursements partly offset capex)
Packaged-goods commodities (nuts, oils, cocoa, dairy) and tariffs

recent_developments.event: Q3 FY2026 results (13 weeks to September 27): net sales $2,304.7M (+4.7%, new stores contributed $128.8M), comps -0.9% (transactions -3.3%, basket +2.5%, cyclospora about -0.6 pt), gross margin 38.2% (-50 bps), EBIT $152.8M, net income $113.4M, diluted EPS $1.21 vs $1.22 (consensus about $1.23, a small miss). Record 15 openings; 504 stores. Operating cash flow YTD $555M, capex YTD $275M.

FY2026 guidance cut: EPS about $4.80 (from $5.32-$5.40), comps about -1.7% (from -0.5% to +0.5%), EBIT about $605M, net sales growth about 4.3%, capex about $310M, 42 net new stores. Q4 guided to comps of -2% to -4% and EPS of $0.47-$0.51 (53rd week adds about $190M sales, $20M EBIT, $0.16 EPS), with about 90 bps of gross margin deleverage from affordability investment.

Stock fell about 23% to a two-year low on the guidance cut. RBC downgraded to Sector Perform (target $49) and BofA downgraded to Underperform (target $47). Before the drop the forward P/E was about 11x (a five-year low); after it, about 8x on one source's estimate. Exact closing price was not confirmed from the sources reviewed.

Strategy reset on the call: management said the current pricing strategy 'has not delivered', and announced increased affordability investments from Q4 FY2026 with a broader price reset in January 2027, plus higher technology, labor and supply chain spending in FY2027. Management committed to maintain EBIT margin above 5% in FY2027 and to adjust the pace based on customer response. No FY2027 unit growth guidance was given.

8-K: Chief Technology Officer James Bahrenburg stepped down effective October 12, 2026, stating no disagreement with the company; he serves as an advisor through March 31, 2027 and remains eligible for severance. No successor was named.

CEO succession announced September 1: President/COO Nick Konat becomes CEO and joins the board on January 4, 2027; Jack Sinclair becomes executive chairman. Sinclair adopted (September 10) a 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 206,896 shares between December 14, 2026 and May 4, 2027. The company crossed 500 stores on September 12. Michael Burry's Scion disclosed a full position in September; Deutsche Bank cut its target to $77 (Hold) on September 25.

Harvest Sherwood litigation settled: the company and the former meat/seafood distributor agreed in principle in June 2026 to settle all claims for an immaterial payment; the bankruptcy court approved it July 27 and payment was made in August. This removes the large litigation overhang described in earlier analyses. Q2 FY2026 (reported July 29): comps -1.0%, EPS $1.37; the stock rose about 9% that day on a JPMorgan upgrade (target $103), which JPMorgan has since cut to $90 (Overweight).

Cyclospora outbreak (lettuce and salad greens) hit produce demand from late Q2 into Q3, costing about 0.6 pt of Q3 comps, with some improvement noted in Q4 to date. Fuel cost headwind added about 10 bps to Q3 gross margin pressure.
Q1 FY2026: comps -1.7% versus +11.7% a year earlier; net sales $2,329M; diluted EPS $1.71 (-6%); first New York State store opened January 2026.

Stock fell about 26% on October 30, 2025 after Q3 FY2025 results and a soft Q4 FY2025 comp guide; securities class action filed November 2025 alleging misleading statements about customer resilience. The stock peaked near $165 in early 2026 and now trades far below that.

items.notes: Prior guide $5.32-$5.40. YTD EPS is $4.30 and the Q4 guide is $0.47-$0.51, which sums to about $4.79, so the $4.80 appears to include the 53rd week (about $0.16); excluding it the underlying 52-week run rate is closer to $4.64. The release labels FY figures 52-week basis, so the DCF should confirm the treatment against the 8-K.
Includes 53rd week impact of about $0.16 EPS, $190M sales and $20M EBIT. Excluding the 53rd week the underlying Q4 is about $0.31-$0.35.
Prior -0.5% to +0.5%. YTD comps are -1.2%; implies Q4 near the guided -2% to -4% range.
Prior path implied flat to slightly positive. Reflects traffic weakness, cyclospora aftermath and the timing of price investment.
Prior 4.5% to 6.5%. Growth is entirely new stores; the 53rd week adds about $190M.
YTD EBIT is $542.3M (down about 4% YoY from $563.1M), so Q4 EBIT is about $63M including about $20M from the 53rd week.
From affordability price investments; shrink and fuel pressure persist into Q4.

While funding price, technology and labor investments; pace subject to customer response. FY2026 guided EBIT margin is roughly 6.4% (605 / about 9,370), so the floor tolerates well over 100 bps of compression.
28 opened and 1 closed YTD. Pipeline: 105 executed leases, over 160 approved sites. No FY2027 target given; CFO signaled the pace must be balanced against other needs of the business.
$301.9M repurchased YTD (3.9M shares at an average $77.65), plus $30M through October 26; $537M remains on the August 2025 authorization.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jack Sinclair attributed the results to 'a challenging consumer environment and the cyclospora disruption' and acknowledged 'the need to improve our performance'. Incoming CEO Nick Konat said affordability is a bigger driver of store choice, that the current pricing strategy has not delivered, and that a more meaningful price investment across a broader range of products (not broad-based discounting) is coming, with a January 2027 reset. CFO Curtis Valentine said investments will be paced to customer response and that EBIT margin should stay above 5% in FY2027; shrink and fuel remain headwinds into Q4.

bull_case: Valuation reset: after a roughly 23% post-earnings drop and a fall of more than 60% from the January 2026 peak, the shares trade near 8-10x forward earnings (one estimate), with zero funded debt and 39-week operating cash flow of about $555M. Mean reversion is possible if the price reset restores traffic.

Management has named the problem and committed to fix it: a broader affordability reset starting Q4 and January 2027, targeting entry-point, produce and key-value items rather than broad discounting, while guarding an above-5% EBIT margin floor in FY2027. Visible price investments could re-engage the less-loyal shopper where leakage is concentrated.
Unit growth continues independent of comps: 42 net new stores in FY2026, a record 15 Q3 openings, 105 signed leases and over 160 approved sites, with new stores adding about $129M to Q3 sales.

Buyback capacity and a net-cash balance sheet: $537M authorization remaining, diluted shares down about 5% YoY, and litigation risk is smaller after the Harvest Sherwood settlement for an immaterial amount.
Structural margin levers remain: completed meat and seafood self-distribution, rising Sprouts Brand mix (about 26%), retail media and loyalty data, and a cyclospora headwind that is fading.
bear_case: The slowdown is not just tough comparisons: transactions are down 3.3-3.4% year to date and management says traffic is not recovering against easier compares; Q4 comps are guided worse at -2% to -4%. Share is moving to Walmart, Costco and Aldi, suggesting a structural price-perception problem.

Earnings are being reset lower with no visibility on the trough: FY2026 EPS guidance cut about 10% to about $4.80 (including a 53rd week), Q4 gross margin faces about 90 bps of deleverage, and FY2027 will carry full-year price, technology and labor investments with only an above-5% EBIT margin floor offered (versus about 6.4% in FY2026).

Price investment is a gamble: management admits the current pricing strategy failed, and tests lifted category sales but not overall traffic; a broad reset risks giving up margin without a comp inflection, and shrink and fuel are already compressing gross margin.

Leadership and execution risk: the CEO handoff on January 4, 2027 coincides with the price reset, the CTO has just left with no successor, and a securities class action over statements on customer resilience is proceeding (amended complaint due November 10, 2026).

Capital intensity and returns: capex rising to about $310M against slightly lower operating cash flow, ROIC down to 16.1% from 18.3%, no FY2027 unit growth guidance, and buybacks done at around $78 per share look poorly timed relative to the current price. Slowing openings would remove the main growth lever.
analysis_note_2026_10_31: Refreshed after the Q3 FY2026 10-Q (filed October 28, 2026), the October 28 earnings release and call, and the October 12 8-K (CTO departure). Material changes versus the 2026-09-28 version: (1) FY2026 guidance cut sharply (EPS about $4.80 vs $5.32-$5.40; comps about -1.7%; EBIT about $605M; Q4 comps -2% to -4%, Q4 EPS $0.47-$0.51); (2) management announced a larger affordability and price reset from Q4 FY2026 into FY2027 with an above-5% FY2027 EBIT margin commitment and no FY2027 unit guidance; (3) the Harvest Sherwood litigation was settled for an immaterial amount (July-August 2026), correcting the prior note which described a pending $1B+ claim; (4) the cyclospora outbreak cost about 0.6 pt of Q3 comps; (5) stock fell about 23% to a two-year low with RBC and BofA downgrades (targets $49 and $47). Earlier notes quoted Q3 EPS guidance of $1.20-$1.24 and an FY comp range of -0.5% to +0.5%; Q3 delivered $1.21 and -0.9%. Caveat: the 52-week vs 53-week basis of the guidance is ambiguous (YTD $4.30 plus Q4 $0.47-$0.51 sums to about $4.79, which suggests $4.80 includes the 53rd week). SFM reports in THOUSANDS. Exact post-drop share price not confirmed.
